plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked schematic shows Turing's 28 May 1936 Universal Computing Machine (U) scanning a single paper tape holding both the encoded rule-table of any machine M and its data bits, alongside the self-referential Halting Problem contradiction matrix proving no algorithm can decide whether an arbitrary program halts.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked diagram on period paper of Turing's 1936 Universal Machine tape (Instruction bits + Data bits on the same strip of 0s and 1s) alongside the self-referential Halting Problem contradiction matrix
teach_overlay.scale: one rule-table small enough to write on a postcard can simulate every piece of software humanity will ever write
